---
title: "SQL Grading Test"
format: live-html
---

This document tests SQL-specific grading behavior for Quarto Live. The focus is on setup execution, checks after user code, positive and negative grading results, SQL error handling, and shared environments.

## Test 1: Correct solution passes check

This test verifies that setup code creates the initial table, the exercise modifies the database state, and the check evaluates the resulting state.

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_insert_pass
#| setup: true
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS numbers_pass;
CREATE TABLE numbers_pass (
 value INTEGER
);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_insert_pass
INSERT INTO numbers_pass VALUES (1), (2), (3);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_insert_pass
#| check: true
SELECT COUNT(*) = 3 AS passed
FROM numbers_pass;
```

Expected result: The check should pass, because the table contains exactly three rows.

## Test 2: Incorrect solution fails check

This test verifies that an incorrect database state leads to negative grading feedback.

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_insert_fail
#| setup: true
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS numbers_fail;
CREATE TABLE numbers_fail (
 value INTEGER
);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_insert_fail
INSERT INTO numbers_fail VALUES (1);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_insert_fail
#| check: true
SELECT COUNT(*) = 3 AS passed
FROM numbers_fail;
```

Expected result: The check should fail, because the table contains only one row instead of three.

## Test 5.4: Check validates inserted values

This test verifies that the check can evaluate not only the number of rows, but also the actual data inserted by the exercise.

````{.markdown filename="sql-functional-test.qmd"}

```{{sql}}
#| exercise: grade_values_pass
#| check: true
SELECT
 COUNT(*) = 3
 AND SUM(price) = 75
 AND MAX(price) = 50
 AS passed
FROM products;
````

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_values_pass
#| setup: true
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS products;
CREATE TABLE products (
 id INTEGER,
 name TEXT,
 price INTEGER
);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_values_pass
INSERT INTO products VALUES
 (1, 'Book', 20),
 (2, 'Pen', 5),
 (3, 'Bag', 50);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_values_pass
#| check: true
SELECT
 COUNT(*) = 3
 AND SUM(price) = 75
 AND MAX(price) = 50
 AS passed
FROM products;
```

Expected result: The check should pass, because the expected rows and values were inserted.

## Test 4: SQL error in solution

This test verifies that an error in the learner solution is detected and reported instead of producing uncaught browser errors.

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_error
#| setup: true
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS error_test;
CREATE TABLE error_test (
 id INTEGER
);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_error
INSERT INTO missing_table VALUES (1);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_error
#| check: true
SELECT COUNT(*) = 1 AS passed
FROM error_test;
```

Expected result: The SQL execution should fail and the error should be shown as feedback.

## Test 5.5: Shared environment grading

This test verifies that checks can evaluate a database state created across multiple exercises in the same shared environment.

```{sql}
#| exercise: shared_grade_1
#| envir: grading_shared
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS shared_numbers;
CREATE TABLE shared_numbers (
 value INTEGER
);
INSERT INTO shared_numbers VALUES (10);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: shared_grade_2
#| envir: grading_shared
INSERT INTO shared_numbers VALUES (20);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: shared_grade_2
#| envir: grading_shared
#| check: true
SELECT COUNT(*) = 2 AS passed
FROM shared_numbers;
```

Expected result: The check should pass, because both exercises use the same shared environment and the table contains two rows.

## Test 6: Shared environment negative grading

This test verifies that shared-environment grading also detects an incorrect state.

```{sql}
#| exercise: shared_grade_fail_1
#| envir: grading_shared_fail
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS shared_fail;
CREATE TABLE shared_fail (
 value INTEGER
);
INSERT INTO shared_fail VALUES (10);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: shared_grade_fail_2
#| envir: grading_shared_fail
INSERT INTO shared_fail VALUES (20);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: shared_grade_fail_2
#| envir: grading_shared_fail
#| check: true
SELECT COUNT(*) = 3 AS passed
FROM shared_fail;
```

Expected result: The check should fail, because the shared table contains two rows instead of three.

## Test 5.6: Check returns numeric result

This test verifies that numeric check results can be interpreted as grading results. A non-zero value should be interpreted as a successful check.

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_numeric_result
#| setup: true
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS numeric_test;
CREATE TABLE numeric_test (
 value INTEGER
);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_numeric_result
INSERT INTO numeric_test VALUES (1), (2);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_numeric_result
#| check: true
SELECT COUNT(*) AS passed
FROM numeric_test;
```

Expected result: The check should pass, because the first result field is a non-zero numeric value.

## Test 5.7: Check returns text result

This test verifies that textual check results such as `ok` can be interpreted as successful grading results.

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_text_result
#| setup: true
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS text_test;
CREATE TABLE text_test (
 value INTEGER
);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_text_result
INSERT INTO text_test VALUES (1);
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_text_result
#| check: true
SELECT
 CASE
   WHEN COUNT(*) = 1 THEN 'ok'
   ELSE 'fail'
 END AS passed
FROM text_test;
```

Expected result: The check should pass, because the first result field contains `ok`.

## Test 9: Check detects missing table

This test verifies that checks fail when the expected database object was not created by the exercise.

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_missing_table
#| setup: true
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS required_table;
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_missing_table
-- The learner solution intentionally does not create the required table.
SELECT 1;
```

```{sql}
#| exercise: grade_missing_table
#| check: true
SELECT COUNT(*) = 1 AS passed
FROM required_table;
```

Expected result: The check should fail with an SQL error, because the expected table does not exist.
